notes:
An audit given five minutes no longer spends twenty-five looking for sitemaps.

A site that asks crawlers to wait thirty seconds between requests, and publishes
a sitemap index listing thirty-nine files, could keep Docket busy for twenty-four
minutes before it fetched a single page. The sitemap step counted how many files
it would read and never how long that would take, and the clock it needed was
already running. It now stops when the time budget does — and so does the
fallback that probes the three conventional sitemap locations, which used to
start up precisely because the first step had been cut short.

When a crawl does run out of time, the advice has stopped blaming the site. It
used to suggest checking the URL, DNS, and firewall or bot protection — on a
server that had just answered forty requests. It now says nothing is blocked,
names the pace the site asked for, and suggests raising the time limit.

Local business schema: a field that is present but empty is now described that
way rather than simply "missing", so somebody who opens their markup and finds
the key sitting there is not left thinking Docket cannot read it.
